# Two planar missed caps, an exposed-source vacancy, and signed affine scope

The independent-axis rank-two obstruction is not automatically preserved
when its unused source parities are filled. There is an exact geometric
reason under an exposed-opposite-fiber hypothesis: two actual missed
caps force the possible source into a barycentric rectangle whose own
depth is too small. The positive-width miss reserve pays the own width
error exactly. This is a concrete restricted parity invariant, not a
general rank-two payment theorem.

There is also a separate arithmetic fact relevant to signed stationarity:
full occupied-source parity forces the source bases to affinely span the
entire sampled base space. Thus the signed affine guard perturbation
cannot be generalized merely by making it vanish at every source.

## 1. Precise exposed-source lemma

Work in continuous dimension two and arbitrary integer dimension. Let
the actual own fiber at base p be a triangle T of area V, with centroid g
and barycentrics lambda_1,lambda_2,lambda_3. Suppose (p,g) is an actual
deepest mark of the pure outward-smoothed problem. Its raw depth Q obeys

    Q>=Gamma_2 V=(4/9)V,                             (1)

because the ordinary centroid bound holds for the own triangle alone.

Let q_minus,q_plus be integer bases with

    p=(q_minus+q_plus)/2,
    K_(q_minus)=D_i=(1-sigma)v_i+sigma T,
    0<sigma<1/3.

Let j,k be the other two vertex indices. Assume there are ACTUAL active
caps at (p,g) with exactly the canonical continuous functionals

    lambda_j-1/3, lambda_k-1/3.

Positive rescaling of their whole equations is allowed. Write their
physical widths in this scaling as w_j=h Gamma(grad lambda_j)>0 and
w_k=h Gamma(grad lambda_k)>0. Assume these two caps miss all of D_i
in the smoothed sense, and have zero outside transition coarea on
K_(q_plus). Finally suppose q_plus is exposed in the COMPLETE sampled
base hull.

Then q_plus cannot be an actual deepest source.

## 2. The two actual misses give a bounded rectangle

Argue by contradiction that q_plus is deepest. The strict actual
source-exclusion identity says that each cap at (p,g) strictly misses
its deepest mark. Zero outside coarea on the positive convex fiber
forces the continuous kernel there to be identically0 or1; the strict
missed-source margin excludes1. Thus both caps miss all of K_(q_plus).

For index j let a_j be the base margin at q_plus, so its base margin at
q_minus is -a_j. Since max_(D_i)lambda_j=sigma, the two smoothed misses
give

    -a_j+sigma-1/3 <=-w_j,
    a_j+max_(Kq)(lambda_j-1/3) <=-w_j.

Eliminating a_j yields

    max_(Kq)lambda_j <= 2/3-sigma-2w_j=:alpha_j.     (2)

The same gives alpha_k=2/3-sigma-2w_k for lambda_k.

Actual convexity gives (D_i+Kq)/2 subset T. Since min_(D_i)lambda_j=0,
min_(Kq)lambda_j>=0; likewise for k. Therefore

    Kq subset {0<=lambda_j<=alpha_j,
               0<=lambda_k<=alpha_k}.              (3)

The barycentric coordinate map (lambda_j,lambda_k) has constant area
Jacobian2V. If either alpha is nonpositive, a positive-area Kq is already
impossible. Otherwise

    |Kq|<=2V alpha_j alpha_k.                        (4)

No assumption that Kq lies inside T is used. The rectangle may cross
lambda_i=0, which is precisely why one must retain all of (3).

## 3. The retained width reserve pays its own smoothing error

At any mark of Kq, one of the ordinary opposite lambda_j cuts has mass
at most |Kq|/2. The lambda_j section density of Kq is bounded by
2V alpha_k, by (3). Averaging the outward displacement over [0,w_j]
adds at most V alpha_k w_j to that selected ordinary cap. Hence

    own smoothed depth at every mark of Kq
       <= |Kq|/2+V alpha_k w_j
       <= V alpha_k(alpha_j+w_j)
       =V(2/3-sigma-2w_k)(2/3-sigma-w_j)
       <V(2/3-sigma)^2
       <(4/9)V.                                    (5)

The first added term uses the mean displacement w_j/2, not a full-width
slab estimate. Either choice of the opposite orientation has the SAME
width by Gamma(-u)=Gamma(u).

Because q_plus is exposed in the complete base hull, a sufficiently
large finite exposing base tilt isolates the selected own cap from
every other sampled fiber. Thus (5) also bounds its MIXED depth. This
contradicts (1), proving the lemma. The argument is exact at positive
width and does not discard an O(h) error.

## 4. What it rules out in a guarded star

Consider the independent-axis base set {0,+-e1,+-e2,+-e3}, keeping T at0
and D_i at -e_i, while allowing the opposite fibers K_(+e_i) to vary
arbitrarily subject to actual convex compatibility. Suppose the middle
centroid remains deepest, the three canonical caps remain actual, the
two complementary caps still miss D_i, and these caps have zero outside
coarea at each possible opposite source.

Every +e_i is exposed. The lemma rules it out as a deepest base. Each
-e_i is also exposed and has total mass sigma^2 V<(4/9)V, so it too is
not deepest. The only source remains0, and all three nonzero occupied
parity classes remain unused. Enlarging the three opposite fibers
therefore cannot fill the source parities while preserving this actual
contact/cap pattern.

In one integer dimension there is a slightly stronger variant. Suppose
the actual fibers at -1 and0 are D_i and T, respectively, and
1/6<sigma<1/3. The two complementary misses at a putative deepest base1
give alpha_j<1/2. Convexity of the minimum lambda_j along the base line,
using its zero values at -1 and0, makes every later minimum nonnegative.
Concavity of the maximum would give max_(K2)lambda_j<=2alpha_j-1<0.
Thus base2 and all larger sampled bases are absent. Similarly convexity
of min lambda_i, equal to1-sigma at -1 and0 at0, would give
min_(K-2)lambda_i>=2(1-sigma)>1, while concavity of its maximum, equal
to1 at both -1 and0, gives max_(K-2)lambda_i<=1. Thus no base-2 exists.
The putative source at1 is exposed automatically, and (5) excludes it.

This is the planar two-cap counterpart of the archived d=4 thin-edge
vacancy theorem, with a different rectangle/depth estimate. Exposure
is essential in arbitrary integer dimension. In particular the earlier
four-base triangle/square construction has an unexposed source at base1
and extra positive outside credit; it does not contradict (5).

## 5. Full source parity forces full affine source span

Let finite P be midpoint-complete in the following lattice sense: if
z,z' in P have equal parity, then (z+z')/2 belongs to P. Let I subset P
meet every parity class occupied by P. Then

    aff(I)=aff(P).                                  (6)

Indeed let A=aff(I). For each z choose a source p(z) of the same parity
and put T(z)=(z+p(z))/2 in P. Because p(z) belongs to A,

    dist(T(z),A)=dist(z,A)/2.

If some z had positive distance, its iterates would give infinitely many
distinct positive distances in the finite set P. This is impossible.
Thus P subset A. This proof needs neither a choice of cap menu nor the
empty-source-polytope property; it retains the original lattice bases.

Consequently any affine base function that vanishes at EVERY deepest
source under full occupied-source parity vanishes at every sampled base.
The single-source replicated-guard rebate Phi=sum z_l, which is zero
on its sole source and antisymmetric on each identical guard pair,
cannot be extended to full source parity by keeping all source terms zero.
Source contributions or a genuinely coupled signed balance must enter.

## 6. Relation to signed stationarity and the remaining gap

The replicated guards are excluded from an actual one-source body
minimum by a signed affine physical response; Optimal's exact path is
saved in `candidate a78d27235a5a2dff`.
Equation (6) identifies a real arithmetic difference in the full-parity
regime, while (2)--(5) show that a naive attempt to add exposed sources
also fails quantitatively before signed stationarity is invoked.

These facts do NOT prove that full source parity forces favorable
retargeting or that every rank-two source then has Gamma capacity.
They leave open nonexposed candidate sources, changed active directions,
and multiple-source signed response conflicts. In particular no separate
per-source affine separator weights are assumed to be common. The
multi-source affine-moment calculation is being developed independently
by Optimal. This note supplies exact geometric and arithmetic constraints
for that calculation rather than restating a general payment inequality.

# Two planar missed caps, an exposed-source vacancy, and signed affine scope

**Parity-complete midpoint closure forces full source affine span**

If every sampled base parity has a deepest source representative and sampled midpoint moves stay in the complete finite base set, repeated midpoint moves halve distance to the affine hull of the source bases. Finiteness forces aff(source bases)=aff(all sampled bases).

Scope limits: This rules out an affine base rebate vanishing on every source but nonzero on another sampled base; it does not supply a common separator or Gamma capacity bound.
